description: Common Cold is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract caused primarily by rhinoviruses. It is characterized by sneezing, nasal congestion, sore throat, and cough. Though generally mild, it can affect daily activities and typically lasts 7–10 days. It is highly contagious and spreads through air droplets and contaminated surfaces.
causes: Exposure to cold or damp weather
Lack of sleep and poor diet
ayurvedic_view: According to Ayurveda, Common Cold is often due to an imbalance in the Kapha and Vata doshas. Kapha increases mucus production, while Vata aggravates dryness and irritation in the respiratory tract.
preventive_measures: Avoid exposure to cold wind and sudden temperature changes
Keep the body warm, especially feet and chest
Consume warm water and herbal teas (Tulsi, Ginger)
Improve immunity with Amla and Chyawanprash

plants_used.usage: Boil 5–6 Tulsi leaves in water. Add a little ginger and honey. Drink twice daily.
Mix ginger juice with honey (1:1) and consume twice a day.
Take 10-15 ml of Amla juice on an empty stomach in the morning.

treatment_methods: Tulsi-ginger tea with honey for sore throat and cough
Amla juice or powder daily to boost immunity
Steam inhalation with eucalyptus oil or tulsi leaves
Gargling with warm saline water
possible_side_effects: Overuse of ginger may cause heartburn
Rare allergic reactions to Tulsi or Amla
Avoid if allergic to any of the herbs used

description: Influenza, commonly known as the flu, is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. It can cause mild to severe illness, and at times can lead to death. The flu is different from a common cold. The flu comes on suddenly. People who have the flu often feel some or all of these symptoms: fever, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle or body aches, headaches, and fatigue. It spreads through air droplets from coughing or sneezing.
causes: Influenza viruses (Type A, B, C, and D)
symptoms: Vomiting and diarrhea (more common in children)
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, influenza is often seen as a result of an imbalance in all three doshas (Vata, Pitta, and Kapha), with a prominent role of Vata due to its rapid onset and body aches. Accumulated Ama (toxins) and weakened Agni (digestive fire) are also contributing factors.
preventive_measures: Maintain good hygiene, including frequent hand washing
Avoid touching eyes, nose, and mouth
Boost immunity through a healthy diet and lifestyle
Avoid crowded places during flu season

plants_used.usage: Consume Guduchi powder (1-3g) with warm water or as a decoction daily.
Chew on a small piece of licorice root or use as a tea for sore throat.
Prepare a decoction of Vasaka leaves and consume twice daily for cough and congestion.

treatment_methods: Herbal teas with ginger, black pepper, and tulsi
Steam inhalation with ajwain (carom seeds) or eucalyptus oil
Light and easily digestible diet (khichdi, vegetable soups)
Warm gargles with turmeric and salt water
Rest and hydration
possible_side_effects: Excessive use of licorice may lead to high blood pressure in some individuals
Guduchi may interact with certain medications; consult a physician if on medication
Rare allergic reactions to any of the herbs

description: Allergic Rhinitis, commonly known as hay fever, is an allergic reaction to airborne allergens such as pollen, dust mites, mold spores, or pet dander. It primarily affects the nose and eyes, causing symptoms similar to a common cold, but it is not caused by a virus. It is characterized by sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, and itchy, watery eyes.
causes: Exposure to airborne allergens (pollen, dust mites, pet dander, mold)
symptoms: Itchy nose, eyes, throat, or roof of mouth
ayurvedic_view: Ayurveda views Allergic Rhinitis as primarily a Kapha disorder, aggravated by Vata. The accumulation of Ama (toxins) in the respiratory channels due to impaired digestion and a weakened immune system is a key factor. Increased Pitta can also lead to burning sensations and redness.
preventive_measures: Keep windows closed during high pollen seasons
Wash bedding and curtains regularly to reduce dust mites
Practice Nasya (nasal oiling) with Anu Taila or sesame oil

plants_used.usage: Mix 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder with warm milk or water and drink daily.
Take Neem leaf powder or capsules as directed, or use a diluted Neem oil for nasal cleansing.
Add freshly ground black pepper to food or make a tea with ginger and honey.

treatment_methods: Neti pot with saline water for nasal cleansing
Herbal formulations containing Trikatu (ginger, black pepper, long pepper)
Dietary changes to reduce Kapha-aggravating foods (dairy, cold foods)
Pranayama (breathing exercises) like Nadi Shodhana
Daily consumption of warm water with honey and lemon
possible_side_effects: Excessive consumption of turmeric may cause stomach upset in some
Neem can be strong; use with caution, especially during pregnancy
Consult an Ayurvedic practitioner for personalized dosages

description: Bronchial Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways characterized by recurrent episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and coughing, particularly at night or in the early morning. These symptoms are usually associated with widespread but variable airflow obstruction within the lung that is often reversible either spontaneously or with treatment.
causes: Environmental allergens (pollen, dust mites, pet dander, mold)
symptoms: Coughing (especially at night or early morning)
Difficulty sleeping due to coughing or wheezing
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, Asthma (Tamaka Shwasa) is primarily a Kapha-Vata disorder. Aggravated Kapha blocks the Vata channels in the respiratory system, leading to constriction and accumulation of mucus. Impaired Agni (digestive fire) and Ama (toxins) also play a crucial role in its pathogenesis.
preventive_measures: Maintain a clean and dust-free environment
Practice yoga and pranayama regularly to improve lung capacity
Consume warm, freshly cooked food; avoid cold and heavy meals
Avoid exposure to cold and damp weather
Regularly clean air filters and humidifiers

plants_used.usage: Take Vasa leaf juice with honey, or as a decoction for cough and breathing difficulties.
Use Pushkarmool powder with honey or warm water, or as part of Ayurvedic formulations.
Consume Bharangi root powder or decoction as recommended by an Ayurvedic practitioner.

treatment_methods: Panchakarma therapies like Vamana (emesis) and Virechana (purgation) under expert guidance
Herbal formulations like Sitopaladi Churna, Talisadi Churna, and Swasakasari Rasa
Warm gargles and steam inhalation
Light, easily digestible, and warm diet; avoid cold, heavy, and processed foods
Regular practice of specific yoga asanas and pranayama (e.g., Bhastrika, Kapalabhati)
possible_side_effects: Self-medication with strong herbs can be risky; always consult an Ayurvedic doctor.
Some herbs may interact with conventional medications; inform your doctor.
Panchakarma therapies require strict adherence to post-therapy regimen.

description: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is a chronic condition that affects the way your body metabolizes sugar (glucose), your body's main source of fuel. With type 2 diabetes, your body either doesn't produce enough insulin, or it resists the effects of insulin. It can lead to serious complications if not managed, including heart disease, nerve damage, kidney disease, and blindness.
causes: Insufficient insulin production by the pancreas
Poor diet (high in processed foods and sugar)
symptoms: Numbness or tingling in the hands or feet
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, Type 2 Diabetes (Madhumeha) is primarily a Kapha disorder, often associated with a sedentary lifestyle and improper diet leading to an accumulation of Ama (toxins). It's also linked to imbalances in Meda Dhatu (fat tissue) and Mutra Vaha Srotas (urinary channels).
preventive_measures: Regular physical activity (at least 30 minutes most days)
Balanced diet rich in whole grains, fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins
Limit intake of sugary drinks and processed foods
Regular health check-ups and blood sugar monitoring

plants_used.usage: Drink fresh bitter melon juice (30-50 ml) on an empty stomach daily.
Soak 1-2 teaspoons of fenugreek seeds overnight in water and consume in the morning. Or, add fenugreek powder to meals.
Take Gymnema leaf powder or capsules as directed, known for 'sugar destroying' properties.

treatment_methods: Dietary management (low glycemic index foods, high fiber)
Regular exercise tailored to individual capacity
Ayurvedic formulations like Chandraprabha Vati, Shilajit, and Karela Jamun juice
Stress reduction techniques (meditation, yoga)
Panchakarma therapies like Virechana (purgation) under expert supervision
possible_side_effects: Bitter melon can cause hypoglycemia if taken with other blood sugar lowering medications
Fenugreek may cause digestive upset or allergic reactions in some individuals
Always consult an Ayurvedic practitioner before starting herbal treatments, especially if on conventional medication.

description: Hypertension, or high blood pressure, is a common condition in which the long-term force of the blood against your artery walls is high enough that it may eventually cause health problems, such as heart disease. It often has no symptoms, earning it the nickname 'the silent killer'.
causes: Certain chronic conditions (e.g., kidney disease, thyroid problems)
ayurvedic_view: Ayurveda describes hypertension as primarily a Pitta and Vata imbalance, often associated with vitiation of Rakta Dhatu (blood tissue). Stress, anger, and improper diet contribute to an increase in Pitta, while Vata imbalance can lead to constriction of vessels.
preventive_measures: Adopt a DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet
Manage stress through meditation, yoga, or deep breathing
Limit alcohol consumption and avoid smoking

plants_used.usage: Take Arjuna bark powder (1-3g) with warm water or milk, or as an Ayurvedic formulation for cardiovascular health.
Consume 1-2 raw garlic cloves daily or use garlic supplements.
Used in traditional Ayurvedic formulations for hypertension (requires expert supervision due to potency and side effects).

treatment_methods: Diet modification (reducing salt, increasing fruits and vegetables)
Regular physical activity and weight management
Stress management techniques (yoga, meditation)
Ayurvedic formulations like Sarpagandha Vati, Punarnavadi Mandur
Abhyanga (oil massage) with specific oils
Panchakarma therapies like Virechana and Basti for Pitta/Vata pacification
possible_side_effects: Sarpagandha is a potent herb and should only be used under strict medical supervision due to potential side effects like drowsiness and nasal congestion.
Garlic can thin blood; caution with anticoagulant medications.
Always consult an Ayurvedic practitioner for proper diagnosis and treatment plan.

description: Migraine is a severe type of headache characterized by throbbing pain, usually on one side of the head. It is often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light and sound. Migraine attacks can cause significant pain for hours to days and can be so severe that they interfere with daily activities.
causes: Certain foods and drinks (e.g., aged cheese, red wine, caffeine withdrawal)
Sensory stimuli (bright lights, loud sounds, strong smells)
Changes in weather or barometric pressure
symptoms: Moderate to severe throbbing head pain (often unilateral)
Auras (visual disturbances like flashing lights or zigzag lines)
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, Migraine (Ardhavabhedaka) is predominantly a Vata and Pitta imbalance. Vata causes the throbbing pain and neurological symptoms, while Pitta contributes to burning sensations, photosensitivity, and irritability. Accumulated Ama can also play a role.
preventive_measures: Eat regular meals to avoid blood sugar drops

plants_used.usage: Take Brahmi powder or capsules regularly for neurological support and stress reduction.
Use Jatamansi powder or oil for calming the nervous system and promoting sleep.
Drink ginger tea at the onset of a migraine attack to help with nausea and pain.

treatment_methods: Shirodhara (oil pouring on the forehead) with specific oils
Nasya (nasal administration of medicated oils) for Vata pacification
Herbal formulations like Shirashooladi Vajra Rasa, Godanti Bhasma
Dietary modifications to avoid Pitta-aggravating foods (spicy, sour, fermented)
Abhyanga (head and foot massage) with specific oils
Yoga and pranayama for stress reduction
possible_side_effects: Some herbs may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery after consumption.
Always consult an Ayurvedic physician for proper diagnosis and personalized treatment, especially for chronic conditions.
Ginger can cause heartburn in some individuals if taken in large quantities.

description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common form of arthritis, affecting millions of people worldwide. It occurs when the protective cartilage on the ends of your bones wears down over time. This can lead to pain, stiffness, and swelling in the affected joints. OA most commonly affects joints in your hands, knees, hips, and spine.
causes: Aging (cartilage naturally wears down over time)
Obesity (puts extra stress on weight-bearing joints)
Repetitive stress on a joint (e.g., from certain occupations or sports)
symptoms: Joint pain (often worse with activity and relieved by rest)
Stiffness (especially after inactivity or in the morning)
Tenderness when pressure is applied to the joint
Loss of flexibility (difficulty moving the joint through its full range of motion)
Grating sensation or clicking sound (crepitus) with joint movement
Bone spurs (hard lumps that form around the affected joint)
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, Osteoarthritis (Sandhivata) is primarily a Vata imbalance. Vata's dry and degenerative qualities lead to the depletion of Asthi Dhatu (bone tissue) and Majja Dhatu (bone marrow), causing dryness and degeneration in the joints. Accumulation of Ama can also contribute.
preventive_measures: Maintain a healthy weight to reduce joint stress
Engage in low-impact exercises (swimming, cycling, walking)
Eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and Vitamin D
Practice proper posture and body mechanics

plants_used.usage: Used in various Ayurvedic formulations for joint pain and inflammation (e.g., Yogaraja Guggul, Maharasnadi Kwath).
Take Boswellia extract or powder as an anti-inflammatory for joint pain.
Use Ashwagandha root powder or capsules to reduce stress and support joint health.

treatment_methods: Abhyanga (warm oil massage) with Vata-pacifying oils (e.g., Mahanarayana Taila)
Swedana (fomentation/steam therapy) to reduce stiffness
Panchakarma therapies like Basti (medicated enema) for Vata pacification
Herbal formulations like Rasnadi Kwath, Maharasnadi Kwath, Yogaraja Guggul
Gentle exercises, yoga, and physical therapy
Dietary changes to reduce Vata (warm, moist, nourishing foods)
possible_side_effects: Guggul can cause mild stomach upset or skin rash in some individuals.
Boswellia is generally well-tolerated but may cause digestive issues.
Always consult an Ayurvedic doctor for appropriate dosage and treatment plan, especially for chronic conditions.

description: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) is a chronic digestive disease in which stomach acid or bile irritates the food pipe lining. This happens when the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) doesn't close properly, allowing stomach contents to flow back into the esophagus. Common symptoms include heartburn and acid regurgitation.
causes: Hiatal hernia (stomach bulges into the chest)
Certain foods and drinks (e.g., spicy foods, fatty foods, caffeine, alcohol, chocolate, citrus)
symptoms: Heartburn (a burning sensation in the chest, often after eating, worse at night or when lying down)
Regurgitation of food or sour liquid
Sensation of a lump in the throat
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, GERD is primarily a Pitta imbalance, often associated with a weakened Agni (digestive fire) and increased Ama (toxins). Excess Pitta leads to acidity and burning sensations, and impaired downward movement of Vata (Apana Vayu) can cause regurgitation.
preventive_measures: Don't lie down for at least 2-3 hours after eating
Elevate the head of your bed

plants_used.usage: Chew on a small piece of licorice root or consume licorice powder mixed with water to soothe the esophagus.
Chew a teaspoon of roasted fennel seeds after meals, or drink fennel tea for digestive relief.
Drink coriander seed water (soaked overnight) or use fresh coriander juice to cool and reduce acidity.

treatment_methods: Dietary modifications (avoiding Pitta-aggravating foods, small frequent meals)
Herbal formulations like Avipattikar Churna, Kamdudha Rasa, Sutshekhar Rasa
Shatavari or Amalaki to soothe irritated membranes
Sheetali and Sitkari pranayama for cooling the body
Virechana (purgation) for Pitta pacification under expert supervision
Mindful eating practices
possible_side_effects: Excessive long-term use of licorice containing glycyrrhizin can lead to elevated blood pressure; DGL (deglycyrrhizinated licorice) is safer for prolonged use.
Always consult an Ayurvedic practitioner for a proper diagnosis and treatment plan, especially for chronic conditions.
Some herbs may interact with conventional antacids or PPIs; inform your doctor.

description: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder that affects the large intestine. Symptoms include cramping, abdominal pain, bloating, gas, and diarrhea or constipation, or both. IBS is a chronic condition that you'll need to manage long term. It doesn't cause changes in bowel tissue or increase the risk of colorectal cancer.
causes: Muscle contractions in the intestine that are stronger or weaker than normal
Inflammation in the intestines (though not true inflammatory bowel disease)
symptoms: Abdominal pain or cramping, often relieved by a bowel movement
Alternating bouts of diarrhea and constipation (IBS-M)
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, IBS (Grahani Roga) is primarily a Vata disorder, affecting Agni (digestive fire) and leading to Ama (toxin) formation. Imbalances in Pitta can manifest as diarrhea or burning, while Kapha can cause sluggish digestion or excessive mucus. The erratic nature of Vata is key to its fluctuating symptoms.
preventive_measures: Identify and avoid trigger foods (e.g., high FODMAP foods, dairy, gluten for some)
Manage stress through yoga, meditation, and mindfulness
Ensure adequate fiber intake, but introduce gradually
Eat regular, smaller meals and eat slowly

plants_used.usage: Mix 1-2 teaspoons of Isabgol husk in warm water or milk, especially useful for IBS-C and IBS-M.
Drink fresh ginger tea or add fresh ginger to meals to aid digestion and reduce bloating.
Chew roasted fennel seeds after meals or drink fennel tea to reduce gas and bloating.

treatment_methods: Dietary modifications (personalized based on dosha and symptoms)
Stress management techniques (Pranayama, meditation)
Herbal formulations like Kutaja Ghan Vati, Bilwadi Churna, Chitrakadi Vati
Panchakarma therapies like Basti (medicated enema) for Vata regulation
Regular intake of buttermilk with a pinch of ginger and cumin
Avoiding cold, raw, and heavy foods
possible_side_effects: Isabgol should always be taken with sufficient water to prevent choking or intestinal obstruction.
Some herbs may cause temporary digestive discomfort as the body adjusts.
Always consult an Ayurvedic practitioner for personalized advice, as IBS management is highly individualized.

description: Hypothyroidism is a condition in which your thyroid gland doesn't produce enough of certain crucial hormones. The thyroid gland is a small, butterfly-shaped gland located at the base of your neck, just below your Adam's apple. Thyroid hormones regulate your metabolism, so an underactive thyroid can slow down many bodily functions, leading to a range of symptoms.
causes: Autoimmune disease (Hashimoto's thyroiditis - most common cause)
Iodine deficiency (less common in iodine-sufficient regions)
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, Hypothyroidism (Galaganda due to Kapha-Vata imbalance) is often considered a Kapha disorder affecting Agni (digestive fire) at both the systemic and cellular levels, leading to sluggish metabolism and accumulation of Ama. Vata imbalance can also contribute to dryness and fatigue.
preventive_measures: Maintain a balanced diet with adequate iodine and selenium (from natural sources)
Avoid raw goitrogenic foods (e.g., raw broccoli, cabbage) in excess

plants_used.usage: Used in formulations like Kanchanar Guggul, known to stimulate thyroid function and reduce Kapha.
Take Ashwagandha root powder or capsules to reduce stress and support endocrine function.
Used for its diuretic and anti-inflammatory properties, often in formulations for edema and metabolic support.

treatment_methods: Panchakarma therapies like Virechana (purgation) and Basti (enema) for Ama elimination and Vata-Kapha balance
Herbal formulations like Kanchanar Guggul, Trikatu, Varunadi Kwath
Dietary adjustments (warm, light, easy-to-digest foods, avoiding cold/heavy/processed foods)
Regular exercise and yoga (especially Surya Namaskar, Sarvangasana)
Stress reduction and lifestyle modifications
possible_side_effects: Guggul can interact with thyroid medications; always consult your doctor before combining treatments.
Ashwagandha can slightly increase thyroid hormone levels; monitor thyroid function if on medication.
Ayurvedic treatment for hypothyroidism requires personalized approach and regular monitoring of thyroid levels.

description: Anxiety disorder is a mental health condition characterized by feelings of worry, nervousness, or unease, typically about an event or something with an uncertain outcome. Unlike occasional anxiety, anxiety disorders involve excessive, intense, and persistent worry and fear about everyday situations, often accompanied by physical symptoms.
causes: Brain chemistry imbalances (neurotransmitters like serotonin, norepinephrine)
Personality factors (certain traits like shyness or perfectionism)
Stressful life events (trauma, loss, chronic illness)
Other medical conditions (e.g., thyroid problems, heart disease)
symptoms: Having a sense of impending danger, panic or doom
Trouble concentrating or thinking about anything other than the present worry
Urge to avoid things that trigger anxiety
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, anxiety (Chitta Udvega / Manovaha Srotas Dushti) is primarily a Vata imbalance, particularly Prana Vata and Vyana Vata, which govern the nervous system and mental functions. Elevated Vata can lead to instability, restlessness, and fear. Pitta can cause irritability, while Kapha can lead to lethargy and attachment.
preventive_measures: Balanced diet, avoiding excessive stimulants (caffeine, sugar)

plants_used.usage: Take Ashwagandha root powder or capsules daily as an adaptogen to reduce stress and anxiety.
Consume Brahmi powder, fresh juice, or capsules to improve cognitive function and reduce anxiety.
Use Jatamansi powder or oil, known for its calming and sedative effects, especially for sleep disturbances related to anxiety.

treatment_methods: Abhyanga (warm oil massage) with Vata-pacifying oils
Shirodhara (oil pouring on the forehead) to calm the mind
Nasya (nasal oiling) with specific oils (e.g., Anu Taila)
Herbal formulations like Saraswatarishta, Smriti Sagar Rasa
Pranayama (breathing exercises like Nadi Shodhana, Bhramari)
Meditation and counseling (Yoga Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy)
Light, warm, grounding diet to balance Vata
possible_side_effects: Some herbs may cause drowsiness; caution is advised when driving or operating machinery.
Always consult an Ayurvedic practitioner before starting herbal remedies, especially if on conventional psychiatric medications.
Self-treatment for anxiety disorders is not recommended; seek professional help.

description: Dermatitis, commonly known as eczema, is a condition that causes skin inflammation, leading to redness, itching, and sometimes blistering or scaling. Atopic dermatitis is the most common and chronic type of eczema, often starting in childhood. It is characterized by dry, itchy skin that can become red, inflamed, and thickened with repeated scratching.
causes: Environmental triggers (allergens like pollen, dust mites, pet dander)
Food allergies or sensitivities (less common in adults)
symptoms: Small, raised bumps which may leak fluid and crust over when scratched
Raw, sensitive, swollen skin from scratching
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, skin conditions like dermatitis (Vicharchika / Kushtha) are primarily a Pitta and Kapha imbalance, often combined with vitiated Rakta Dhatu (blood tissue) and Ama (toxins). Pitta contributes to inflammation, redness, and burning, while Kapha leads to oozing, itching, and stickiness. Vata can cause dryness and scaling.
preventive_measures: Moisturize skin regularly with natural emollients
Avoid harsh soaps and detergents; use mild, fragrance-free products
Take lukewarm baths/showers and pat dry
Maintain a balanced diet and stay hydrated

plants_used.usage: Apply diluted Neem oil topically, or take Neem leaf powder/capsules for its purifying properties.
Apply a paste of turmeric and neem to affected areas, or consume turmeric with warm milk for internal purification.
Take Manjistha powder or extract as part of Ayurvedic formulations for blood purification and skin health.

treatment_methods: Panchakarma therapies like Virechana (purgation) for Pitta and Ama elimination
Local application of medicated oils (e.g., Mahamarichyadi Taila, Jatyadi Taila)
Herbal formulations like Arogyavardhini Vati, Kaishore Guggul, Khadirarishta
Dietary modifications (avoiding spicy, sour, fermented, and incompatible foods)
Stress management techniques
External cleansing with herbal decoctions
possible_side_effects: Topical application of some herbs may cause temporary stinging or irritation in sensitive individuals.
Internal use of blood-purifying herbs may require guidance, especially if on other medications.
Manjistha can sometimes temporarily turn urine reddish-brown, which is harmless.

description: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disorder that can affect more than just your joints. In some people, the condition can damage a wide variety of body systems, including the skin, eyes, lungs, heart and blood vessels. Unlike the wear-and-tear damage of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis affects the lining of your joints, causing painful swelling that can eventually result in bone erosion and joint deformity.
causes: Autoimmune response (immune system attacks its own tissues)
Genetic predisposition (certain gene markers like HLA-DR4)
symptoms: Tender, warm, swollen joints (often small joints of hands and feet)
Rheumatoid nodules (firm lumps under the skin)
ayurvedic_view: In Ayurveda, Rheumatoid Arthritis (Amavata) is considered a complex condition caused by vitiated Vata combined with Ama (undigested toxins). Ama accumulates in the joints and channels, obstructing circulation and causing inflammation and pain. Pitta can also be involved, leading to burning, while Kapha can cause swelling and stiffness.
preventive_measures: Balanced, anti-inflammatory diet (avoiding processed foods, refined sugar)

plants_used.usage: Used in Ayurvedic formulations like Yogaraja Guggul, Maharasnadi Kwath, known for their anti-inflammatory and Ama-reducing properties.
Consume Giloy juice, powder, or decoction for its immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects.
Used in various Ayurvedic formulations for joint pain and inflammation, particularly for Vata disorders.

treatment_methods: Langhana (fasting) or light diet to reduce Ama
Deepana-Pachana (kindling digestive fire and digesting Ama) with herbs like ginger, pippali
Panchakarma therapies (Virechana, Basti, Swedana) tailored to individual needs
Abhyanga (warm oil massage) with specific medicated oils (e.g., Mahanarayana Taila, Mahamasha Taila)
Herbal formulations like Amavatari Rasa, Rasnadi Guggul, Simhanada Guggul
Specific yoga asanas and gentle exercises to maintain joint mobility
Avoiding incompatible food combinations (Viruddha Ahara)
possible_side_effects: Some herbs can interact with conventional immunosuppressants or NSAIDs; consult your doctor.
Panchakarma therapies require strict adherence to dietary and lifestyle guidelines post-therapy.
Ayurvedic treatment for RA is complex and requires guidance from an experienced practitioner.
